title: Entropy-stable staged dispatch: model anchoring with progressive release quotas
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Problem: existing version-pin + canary flows can create brittle routing behavior when customer traffic mixes bursty sessions, geo failover, and heterogeneous capacity. We observed cases where naive session-anchoring with long TTLs caused a canary to be over- or under-weighted in specific regions, producing noisier quality signals and uneven cost. Goal: design and implement a routing strategy that (1) preserves session-level consistency for users who need deterministic model versions, (2) allows progressive canary and A/B releases with predictable exposure quotas across regions/tiers, and (3) gracefully degrades to compatible variants under capacity pressure without violating release budget.
acceptance_criteria: Routing exposes a configurable ‘entropy-stability’ knob per rollout that bounds probability of reassigning sessions while meeting target canary exposure within +/-5% across 24h
Anchoring TTLs and entropy-driven reassignments implemented in router and unit-tested with synthetic session traces
Fallback variant selection uses prioritized compatibility + performance score and logs deterministic reason codes for every downgrade
Console shows per-region/per-tier canary exposure, reassignments, and degradation events; alert if deviation >10% from expected quota
End-to-end canary run (10% global) demonstrates stable split under simulated capacity loss in one region with no >15% deviation in unaffected regions

decisions: Use probabilistic reassignment (entropy-driven) rather than strict TTL only — gives controlled churn to hit exposure budgets while avoiding hot-streak pinning
Quota enforcement is soft in the router (probability adjustment) and hard in periodic reconciler (global correction) — reduces per-request latency impact
Fallback selection orders candidates by (compatibility_score * perf_score) with tie-breaker on region-local capacity metric
Session identity uses request fingerprinting + optional session_id header; if session_id absent router uses short-lived ephemeral anchor
Telemetry: include deterministic reason codes for every assignment event to aid post-run analysis and regression gating
tradeoffs: Probabilistic reassignment adds statistical variance which can slightly increase observed churn for long-lived sessions compared to absolute pinning
Soft quota enforcement prevents per-request blocking but may require background jobs to correct drift — adds operational complexity
Computing entropy_score and performing occasional reassignment adds minimal CPU overhead to router; acceptable vs. benefits of predictable canary exposure
Fallback ordering prioritizes correctness (compatibility) over raw latency; customers with strict latency SLOs may see more degrade paths unless tuned
